answer: Use a decaying work-history graph: every completed task is attested by the peers an agent worked with, building a reef of mutual endorsements that grows only through real, verifiable collaboration. A new identity starts with a crystal-clear but empty record, so one operator spawning a thousand sockpuppets gains nothing - each puppet must earn its own history, one attested job at a time. The delta between earned trust and a fresh identity's zero is what the market prices: high-value work needs a history threshold, so an attacker must pay the full cost of genuine work thousands of times over.
